w10_T4_001379: A market stall records its takings in whole dollars rather than in cents. On each of 9 market days the stall took 202 dollars, and it all went into one cash box. Rent for the pitch cost 1518 dollars and a new awning cost 15 dollars, both paid out of the box. The stall is 3 metres wide. Over the following season the box grew to 6 times what it was holding. How many dollars are in the cash box now?
w10_T4_001382: A toy factory made 9 batches of wheels, with 179 wheels in every batch. The wheels were shared equally between the 3 assembly lines, and one line took its share. The factory employs 60 people. The same number of wheels was then sent to each of the 4 shifts working that week. Over the month 1102 of those wheels were fitted to toy cars. How many wheels are left?
w10_T4_001389: A school office keeps all of its photocopies in one paper tray. On Monday morning the copier ran 8 batches of 207 sheets each into that tray. Before lunch 123 sheets were taken out for a test. In the afternoon the office ordered enough copies for the tray to hold 9 times as many sheets as it did. That evening a teacher added 40 sheets she had copied herself. The trust now wants 3 offices with trays holding as many sheets as this one. How many sheets will the 3 offices hold?
w10_T4_001398: A charity walk records its sponsorship in whole dollars rather than in cents. On the first day 31 dollars were pledged and 45 dollars more came in by the evening. A company then promised to make the fund 9 times as large as it was. Printing costs of 66 dollars were taken out of the fund. The walk covers 26 kilometres. A second company made the fund 3 times as large again, and two walkers added 53 dollars and then 31 dollars of their own. How many dollars are in the fund now?
w10_T4_001399: A radio station logs its advertising in minutes rather than in seconds, and keeps one running total. On a typical day each of its 5 shows carries 15 minutes of adverts. The station ran that same pattern on each of 4 days last week. A sponsor then added 10 minutes to the total, while an advertiser cancelled 61 minutes. A charity was given 9 minutes on the same total. The station now plans 5 weeks with exactly that total. How many minutes of advertising does the plan come to?
w10_T4_001402: A tool library keeps all of its cordless drills on one rack. The rack held 61 drills, and a donation added 4 more. Over the spring 51 drills were lent out and never returned, and 13 more were found to be broken and were scrapped. In the summer a hardware shop gave the library 28 drills, and a repair workshop returned 14 that had been mended. One drill was then sold at the open day. How many drills are on the rack now?
w10_T4_001404: On Friday morning a campsite shop had 13 gas bottles in the yard, and 6 of them were empty and went back to the supplier. In the afternoon a delivery tripled the number of bottles in the yard. That evening a wholesaler dropped off 65 more bottles. On Saturday 23 bottles were sold to campers. How many gas bottles are in the yard now?
w10_T4_001407: A stationer counts its invitations in single cards rather than in boxes. A wedding order was printed as 9 runs of 171 cards each. A faulty press spoiled 783 of the cards and they were pulped. The rest were shared equally between the 4 families involved, and one family took its share home, where half of the cards were found to be printed in gold ink. That family has now ordered 6 sets of the same size for other events. How many cards will that order come to?
w10_T4_001412: A solar company keeps all of its panels in one depot. A delivery brought 8 lorries carrying 152 panels each. A housing job then took 458 panels from the depot. The company restocked so that the depot held 7 times as many panels as were left. An installer returned 16 panels that would not fit. A school roof used 564 panels and a factory roof took another 3879. How many panels are in the depot now?
w10_T4_001415: A beekeeper filled 180 jars with honey during the summer. 140 of the jars were sold at the farmers' market. A neighbour returned 3 jars that had not been opened, and half of her jars carry a blue label. In the autumn 34 jars were given away as gifts and 4 were dropped and broken. She now plans 7 hives, each producing as many jars as she has left. A friend then gave her 4 filled jars from his own hive. How many jars of honey will she have?
w10_T4_001426: On Saturday morning a greengrocer had 195 melons on the stall. By lunchtime 192 of them had been sold to a hotel. In the afternoon the wholesaler delivered enough melons for the stall to hold 4 times as many as were left. That evening 7 melons were sold, and on Sunday another 3 went. How many melons are on the stall now?
w10_T4_001428: A decorating warehouse keeps all of its wallpaper rolls in one bay. The bay held 236 rolls, and a returned order added 13 more. The manager then ordered enough for the bay to hold 9 times as many rolls as it did. A national contract made the bay hold 4 times that number. Half of the rolls in the bay are patterned. A supplier finally added 17 sample rolls to the same bay. How many rolls are in the bay now?
w10_T4_001430: A call centre logs its calls in minutes rather than in seconds, and keeps one running total for each team. On Monday morning one team's total stood at 178 minutes, and 51 minutes were struck off because of a recording fault. In the afternoon that team handled 6 times as many minutes as its total showed. That evening the figure for the whole floor came to 9 times the team's total, since 9 teams worked the same hours. The company's 9 sites all worked to exactly that pattern. How many minutes did the company log?
w10_T4_001437: Petra picks more punnets of strawberries than her workmate Josef does. The cold room held 140 punnets, and Petra brought in 52 more. The farm then filled the room to 4 times that number for the weekend market. The farm covers 12 hectares. Over the weekend 325 punnets were sold, and on Monday Josef added 80 punnets he had picked. How many punnets are in the cold room now?
w10_T4_001438: A coach company records its fares in whole dollars rather than in cents, and keeps one takings box. The box held 97 dollars on Monday, and Tuesday's trip added 66 dollars. A school booking then made the box hold 4 times as much as it did. A passenger paid 4 dollars for a late seat. A matching grant doubled everything in the box. How many dollars are in the takings box now?
w10_T4_001454: On Monday morning a school stockroom took in 8 boxes of exercise books, with 25 books in each box. By the afternoon the supplier had delivered 9 times that many books for the whole year group. That evening the order was repeated for each of the 6 year groups in the school. A teacher added 49 books left over from last year and a parent donated 53 more. The school has 14 science labs. During the year 3927 books were handed out to pupils. How many exercise books are left in the stockroom?
w10_T4_001456: A florist had 115 metres of ribbon on the roll. 98 metres were used on a wedding order and 9 metres were spoiled by a wet floor. The supplier then sent 9 times as much ribbon as was left. Half of that ribbon was sent on to the shop's second branch. The florist bought 4 times as much again for the Christmas season, and a wholesaler then supplied 4 times that amount for the whole chain. How many metres of ribbon does the chain have?
w10_T4_001464: A veterinary clinic counts its vaccine in single doses rather than in vials, and Dr Alvarez orders more of it than Dr Novak does. The fridge held 231 doses, and a delivery added 58 more. The health board then supplied 7 times that many doses for the county campaign. A neighbouring clinic sent over 50 doses it could not use, and a supplier added 26 doses as a sample. How many doses does the campaign have?
w10_T4_001471: On Monday morning a playground project had 43 bags of wood chips on site, and a second lorry doubled that number before lunch. In the afternoon a supplier delivered 58 more bags. On Tuesday the council sent 35 bags. On Wednesday evening a landscaper dropped off another 58. How many bags of wood chips are on site now?
w10_T4_001475: A bicycle workshop keeps all of its spokes in one bin. The bin held 224 spokes, and a repair job put 21 more back into it. The wholesaler then filled the bin to 7 times that number. A customer donated 60 spokes from an old wheel, and a colleague added 73. The workshop is open 5 days a week. The chain now wants 6 workshops with bins holding as many spokes as this one. How many spokes will the 6 workshops need?
w10_T4_001476: A print shop ordered 7 cases of ink cartridges, each case holding 200 cartridges. Over the year 1324 cartridges were used in the machines and 64 were found to be dried out. The shop has 11 printers. The supplier then delivered 3 times as many cartridges as were left. Head office repeated that order 3 times over for the whole group. A customer returned 35 unopened cartridges. How many cartridges does the shop have now?
w10_T4_001479: A juice press keeps all of its bottles in one chilled room. On Monday morning 6 crates were carried in, each holding 223 bottles. Before lunch a farm added 37 bottles to the same room. During the afternoon 1077 bottles were loaded onto vans for the shops. Half of the bottles in the room are apple juice. That evening a cancelled order put 65 bottles back into the chilled room. How many bottles are in the chilled room now?
w10_T4_001484: A museum shop counts its pencils one by one rather than by the box. The tray held 204 pencils, and 181 were sold during the half-term week. A further 4 were snapped by visitors and thrown away. The shop has 7 windows. The buyer then ordered enough pencils for the tray to hold 8 times as many as were left. A school returned 23 pencils it had not needed. How many pencils are in the tray now?
w10_T4_001490: On Monday morning a farm carted in 7 loads of hay, each load holding 223 bales. In the afternoon a neighbour delivered 44 bales and a contractor added 40 more. Half of the bales were stacked at the back of the barn. That evening 265 bales were sold to a stables. Over the winter the cattle ate 1254 bales. How many bales are left in the barn?
w10_T4_001491: A cinema records its takings in whole dollars rather than in cents. Each of the 7 screenings took 86 dollars, and all of it went into one safe. Half of the money in the safe was banked the next morning. Wages of 187 dollars were then paid out of the safe. What was left was shared equally between the 3 partners who own the cinema, and one partner put her share in an envelope, to which she added 69 dollars of her own. How many dollars are in her envelope?
